the brightness pyrometer is an efficient instrument for measuring the temperature of substances in the liquid phase upon fast heating with a microcurrent pulse.
the temperature measurement with a brightness pyrometers is possible only in a narrow temperature interval (from 1000 to 2500°C) and only for materials with low thermal conductivity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a pyrometer can be used to measure temperature of materials upon fast heating with a micro-second electric current pulse, provided that the temperature of the material is not too high (less than 2500°C) and the material is not very reflective (less than 20% reflectance).
the method developed is suitable for measuring temperatures of metals, carbide, and graphite in the range 1000-5000 K.
the temperature measurement method proposed is applicable to the temperature measurement of conducting materials with high heat capacity upon heating with a short electric current pulse.
